newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends up at two-year high vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends up at two-year high vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended up at a two-year high close of 8.2910 on Friday from Thursday's 8.2914 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai due to speculative buying late in the session, traders said.
The close was the highest from May 18, 1995 when the yuan ended at 8.2892.
The weighted average price on Thursday was 8.2925.
Dealers said speculative buying emerged late in trading to push up the yuan with the People's Bank, the central bank, taking no action to depress it.
The yuan opened slightly down at 8.2915 and fell slowly to hit an intraday low of 8.2919 early in trading.
It then began to rise and moved around 8.2915 for most of the session before pushing up even further late in trading, hitting a high of 8.2864.
Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2914, traders said.
One dealer said the central bank did not intervene to prevent the yuan's upward trend on Friday, encouraging buying late in the session.

"The market had been worried about possible central bank intervention," he said. "As the yuan rose today, the bank took no action. This boosted pro-yuan setiment and encouraged buying late in trading."
A second dealer said thin volume ahead of the weekend exaggerated the yuan's rise today. "The yuan is expected to face heavy selling pressure early next week," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to test the key 8.2900 resistance level early next week.
The yuan closed up at 7.2510 from 7.3100 against 100 Japanese yen and higher at 1.0705 from 1.0715 against the Hong Kong dollar.
